A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same contribution-classification study, taxonomy, and corpora. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original annotation results, classifier evaluations in Table 4, and analyses of contribution trends, publication venues, and citations in Section 5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports contribution-type-specific classifier scores and citation distributions in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The eight-category taxonomy, binary-relevance classification, fine-tuned and prompted model approaches, and SciBERT corpus-labeling procedure remain unchanged. The prompts in v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 11 match.

E1.justification: Both versions use 1,995 annotated abstracts, 28,937 ACL Events papers from 1974 to February 2024, and the same ACL 2017 and 2018 citation samples. The recent-years discussion uses existing coverage; Section 7's proposed applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 4 retains the same random, fine-tuned, and prompted comparators. PubMedBERT is renamed BiomedBERT consistently with the existing methods description. The few-shot comparison also retains the same three LLMs.

E3.justification: The paper-level 70/15/15 split, hyperparameter grid, batch size, and prompting settings are unchanged. However, v2 Section 5.1 Q1 describes percentages of contribution statements, whereas v1 explicitly aggregates papers. Figure 2 still measures percentages of papers, leaving unclear whether the aggregation protocol changed or its description became inaccurate.

E4.justification: V2 adds a diagnostic breakdown of SciBERT performance by contribution type (Table 7) and citation-distribution analysis (Figure 9). Existing few-shot comparisons, venue analyses, and abstract-length checks remain. Appendix A.1 discusses recent trends using the existing Figure 3 rather than introducing a new experiment.

E5.justification: Figure 9 extends descriptive statistical reporting beyond citation means and medians to boxplots showing spread and outliers. The three classifier runs, variance below 0.02, annotation-agreement confidence bounds, and McNemar significance threshold remain unchanged. The boxplots do not establish additional runs or inferential confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V2 adds per-type SciBERT F1 scores of 0.80–0.81 and citation-distribution results; corresponding aggregate classifier, few-shot, and citation tables retain their values. It also introduces a reporting inconsistency: Q1 states 89.8% for k-task, while the unchanged Figure 2 bar is approximately 96%.

T1.justification: The label-indicator formulation in Section 4.1 and the contribution definitions in the annotation guidelines are unchanged. Moving the definitions from Appendix A to Appendix C introduces no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The core taxonomy, dataset, task, and field-analysis contributions remain. The abstract shifts the stated revival of language and human-centered research from post-2020 to the late 2010s, foregrounds increasingly multifaceted contributions, and adds potential utility for literature-survey generation.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds explanations connecting recent trends to LLM capability testing, multilingual weaknesses, and bias mitigation. Section 3.3 qualifies co-occurrence as low overall, with relatively higher k-people/k-task association. Section 7 expands possible applications, while the principal corpus, abstract-only, and classifier-accuracy limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents senior-author review of annotations, particularly disagreements, in Section 3.2 and updates the supplied code/data repository address. This is additional documentation, not evidence that the underlying annotation or training procedures were newly changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on scientific leaderboard extraction, argument mining, key-point analysis, recent NLP developments, and literature-support applications. It retains the central distinction from NLPContributionGraph and citation-intent research, so the research positioning is expanded without being fundamentally redefined.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, related work, results, and conclusion, organizing findings into labeled points. It adds Applications and Future Work, moves two main-text venue questions into Appendix A, and reorganizes the annotation guidelines and supplementary results.

P2.justification: V2 relocates the taxonomy table and venue figures, enlarges displays, revises captions and legend placement, and adds Table 7 and Figure 9. Figures 10–12 provide large grouped redisplays of the previously cramped venue trajectories, substantially changing their readability without adding new trajectories.

improvement.justification: The clearer results organization, enlarged venue plots, per-type classifier scores, and citation boxplots modestly improve readability and transparency. The gains are tempered by new Q1 reporting inconsistencies, including the ambiguous aggregation unit and the k-task percentage that conflicts with Figure 2. The core empirical evidence remains largely unchanged.
